name: Miami
operatingHours: Metrorail (Green and Orange Lines) runs ~5:00 AM–~12:00 AM daily, every ~10 min at peak and 15–30 min evenings and weekends. The free Metromover loops around Downtown and Brickell ~5:00 AM–~12:00 AM. No rail reaches Miami Beach: take Metrobus routes 119/120 (Beach Max) or the free Miami Beach Trolley.
fareInfo: Tap a contactless card or phone at the Metrorail gates or bus farebox (or use an EASY Card or the GO Miami-Dade Transit app); fares are capped at $5.65 a day. Metrorail ~$2.65 and Metrobus $2.25 per ride under the Feb 2026 fare guide; 1-day pass $5.65, 7-day $29.25. Metromover and the city and Miami Beach trolleys are free. No cash at Metrorail gates.

sights.name: Wynwood Walls
sights.note: An outdoor gallery of huge murals by international street artists, set among converted warehouses in the heart of Wynwood's galleries and breweries.
sights.hours: ~11:00 AM–7:00 PM daily (to ~8:00 PM Fri–Sat); timed tickets

sights.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
sights.note: A 1916 Italian Renaissance-style winter villa on Biscayne Bay, with furnished rooms, formal gardens and a stone barge in the water.

sights.name: Little Havana (Calle Ocho)
sights.note: The heart of Cuban Miami along SW 8th Street, with Domino Park, cigar rollers, cafecito windows and live salsa at night.
sights.hours: Neighbourhood, always open; Domino Park ~9:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: Miami Design District
sights.note: A few blocks of designer flagships, public art and architecture, including the Buckminster Fuller dome and the free Institute of Contemporary Art.
sights.hours: Streets always open; shops ~11:00 AM–7:00 PM

sights.name: Bayfront Park
sights.note: A downtown waterfront park on Biscayne Bay with Isamu Noguchi landscaping, a concert amphitheatre and views of the cruise port.

sights.name: Coconut Grove
sights.note: Miami's oldest neighbourhood, a leafy bayside village of sidewalk cafes, marinas and the CocoWalk plaza.

sights.name: Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science
sights.note: A science museum in Museum Park with a three-level aquarium, a planetarium and hands-on exhibits.

sights.name: Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM)
sights.note: Modern and contemporary art in a Herzog & de Meuron building with hanging gardens and a shaded bayfront terrace.
sights.hours: Thu–Mon 11:00 AM–6:00 PM (Thu to 9:00 PM); closed Tue–Wed

sights.name: Ocean Drive and the Art Deco Historic District
sights.note: South Beach's oceanfront strip of pastel 1930s Art Deco hotels, neon signs and sidewalk cafes, busiest after dark.

sights.name: Lummus Park Beach
sights.note: The classic stretch of South Beach sand in front of Ocean Drive, with the colourful lifeguard towers and a beachfront path.
sights.hours: Beach open daily; lifeguards ~9:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: South Pointe Park
sights.note: A grassy park and pier at the southern tip of Miami Beach, where cruise ships pass through Government Cut at sunset.

sights.name: Lincoln Road
sights.note: A pedestrian mall designed by Morris Lapidus, lined with shops, outdoor restaurants and the New World Symphony's concert hall.
sights.hours: Street always open; shops ~10:00 AM–10:00 PM

sights.name: Española Way
sights.note: A short Mediterranean Revival lane of 1920s arcades and outdoor restaurants just off Washington Avenue.

sights.name: Holocaust Memorial Miami Beach
sights.note: A free open-air memorial centred on a vast bronze arm reaching skyward, with a reflecting pool and a wall of names.

sights.name: Miami Beach Boardwalk
sights.note: A boardwalk running behind the dunes from 21st Street north for about 3 km, good for an ocean-side walk or jog away from the crowds.

railStations.name: MiamiCentral
railStations.note: Downtown hub for Brightline trains to Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach and Orlando (~3h30m), and for Tri-Rail commuter trains; Metrorail's Government Center and Historic Overtown stations and the Metromover are connected. Amtrak's Silver Meteor uses Miami Airport Station instead.
railStations.hours: Station ~5:00 AM–~12:00 AM; Brightline ~5:00 AM–~11:00 PM to its timetable. Metrorail ~5:00 AM–~12:00 AM.

airports.name: Miami International Airport
airports.transitNote: The free MIA Mover train from the terminal's 3rd level reaches Miami Airport Station in ~4 min, where Metrorail's Orange Line (on the map) runs to Government Center/Downtown in ~15 min. For South Beach, the 150 Miami Beach Airport Express bus takes ~45 min (not on the map). Fort Lauderdale (FLL) is the other airport many visitors use, ~45 min north by Brightline or Tri-Rail plus a shuttle.
airports.hours: Metrorail Orange Line: first ~5:00 AM, last ~11:40 PM. MIA Mover runs 24 h.
